rv.q: Edmundson’s version is faithful but overstuffed, cramming in themes of charity, class, inheritance and sex trafficking.
In the end, the richness of the incidental detail more than compensates for the over-complicated narrative.
Despite some reservations, this remains a mostly engrossing adaptation of an important book, with some glorious music and a large cast telling an important and much-loved story.

cn.t: Critics find Coram Boy an engrossing but overstuffed epic — strong performances and soaring choral music impress, though its sprawling plot strains dramatic focus.
